decisions.question: The analyzer queues override tasks only for methods carrying @Override. Most real Java omits the annotation (clojure/ASF code) — are un-annotated overrides relationships?
decisions.resolution: Yes — JLS 8.4.8: @Override is a compile-time check, not a requirement; an un-annotated instance method whose signature matches an accessible ancestor method overrides it. Two-corpus gate wave 2026-09 (clojure:java SubVector.iterator). The analyzer now queues implicit tasks for every non-static, non-private, non-constructor instance method, but emits ONLY on a verified exact-signature in-file match (pass 1). Explicit @Override tasks alone keep the companion-index (pass 2) and first-parent guess (pass 3) tiers, so overloads never fabricate.

decisions.question: The override TRUTH pairs by method NAME only — same-name-different-signature overloads (SubVector.nth(int) vs APersistentVector.nth(int, Object)) were asserted as overrides. Signature-exact?
decisions.resolution: Yes. Two-corpus gate wave 2026-09: the shared oracle collected members with the return type / nested-type-name bugs (the /identifier/ test matched type_identifier first and the field_declaration|declaration guard swallowed method_declaration AND let nested class_declaration through). All fixed: method names come from the grammar name field, member collection is field_declaration-only for variables with nested type nodes excluded, and override pair emission is signature-aware (parameter-type signature overlap required when both sides record signatures). Private ancestor methods never pair (JLS 8.4.8.1).

decisions.question: M37.21 #610 user-suspect wave: methods inside anonymous bodies were attributed to the enclosing class (contains Service->compare on the probe) and no symbol existed for the anonymous type.
decisions.resolution: Mirror the kotlin family convention: anonymous_<SuperName> Class symbol (noise name, never leaks into the index), ownerName = enclosing type, scope pushed for the class_body so members attribute to the anonymous type (contains anonymous_Comparator->compare). object_creation_expression handler pushes the scope; exit-scheduling is the walk's uniform tail. Fixture java/anonymous-and-multihop-overrides pins both directions (expect + forbid contains Service->compare/run); mutants java/anonymous-body-scope-leak + java/override-multihop-bare-name.

decisions.question: M37.21 #610 clojure PersistentTreeMap: overrides through a NON-declaring ancestor (BlackVal.val -> Node.val, Black declares no val) were lost — classHierarchy is FQN-keyed but parents are bare leaf names, so hop-2 looked up classHierarchy with the bare name and missed.
decisions.resolution: Suffix-resolve every bare parent name to its FQN candidate(s) during the BFS; symbolMap method-symbol hits disambiguate same-named classes. JLS 8.4.8.1 nearest-declaring-ancestor semantics unchanged (BFS level-by-level, private-ancestor skip). Both java lanes 100%/0/0 at 200 files after the fix.

decisions.question: M37.21 #610 user-suspect: method_invocation targets collapse overloads to the bare leaf name (callExpression.split('.').pop()) — two same-name overloads are indistinguishable.
decisions.resolution: Deliberate contract: the universal call graph is name-leaf based family-wide (java/kotlin/scala/groovy/php/ruby/python all emit leaf targets); overload signature matching requires type inference the tree-sitter layer does not have. Recorded so a downstream consumer needing overload identity knows the boundary. Not a defect.

decisions.node_type: syntax-error reporting (ERROR/MISSING vs hasError on typed nodes)
decisions.question: Hygiene: only ERROR/MISSING nodes push errors; hasError on a WELL-TYPED node (a method containing one bad child) is silent
decisions.decision: Ruled intentional: a typed node with an embedded error still ANALYZES correctly (tree-sitter recovery keeps the valid subtree); pushing a file-level error per bad child would flood output on generated/amalgamated files. The C-wave guarantee (error-containing files still emit recoverable content) is the standing probe. receiver_parameter (skip-listed) joins the documented skip set — receiver params (void m(Outer this)) are receiver binders, not user parameters

decisions.question: Hygiene: symbolMap.set(name, sym) bare overwrite lets nested same-name classes (Outer.Inner vs Other.Inner) repoint the alias
decisions.decision: Set-if-absent (first-wins). Verified: the only symbolMap.get is FQN-keyed (override BFS), so bare keys are informational and can never misresolve — the fix removes the silent-repoint hazard

decisions.question: Hygiene: finalFrameworks[0] depended on import order — same file could report spring_mvc or spring depending on which import came first
decisions.decision: Deterministic pickJavaFramework: fixed priority list (spring_data > spring_mvc > spring_core > spring > jpa > hibernate > ...), alphabetical tiebreak. No fixture pinned framework (verified), lanes unaffected

decisions.question: M49 R3 claim 1: overloads collapse to the same bare leaf target (process(String) vs process(int) both -> process) and even metadata carried no discriminator
decisions.decision: Bare-leaf target STAYS the matching contract (JD20; oracle mirrors it) but every calls edge now carries metadata.argumentCount (named children of argument_list) — additive payload; downstream consumers can disambiguate by arity without a resolution engine. Probe: process sites carry argumentCount=1, other.a.b carries 3. Fixture overload-arity-varargs-multicatch pins; mutants java/drop-arity-payload + java/varargs-sig-not-normalized (348/348). Claims 2+3 verified-working and pinned: JLS 8.4.1 int.../int[] equivalence resolves both cross combinations exact-in-file (was true by construction, unproven until this probe); multi-catch unions emit declared_type for EVERY member

decisions.question: The override resolver has three tiers. Pass 1 resolves by exact signature against an in-file ancestor (1.0, `exact-in-file`); pass 2 handles generic substitution (0.9); pass 3 fires when neither applies — the declaring ancestor lives in another compilation unit, so from this file alone it is unknowable — and names the FIRST hierarchy parent at 0.5. Pass 3 is justified in the code by reasoning: 'the explicit @Override annotation asserts intent'. Is that justification sufficient, and what is its actual error rate?
decisions.decision: RULED — the tier STAYS, and its justification is replaced by a measurement. The reasoning was true but unquantified, which is not the same as verified. Measured on grails-core (60-file draw, every guess checked against a repo-wide index of 2,157 type declarations built from 1,942 files): 82 guess edges — 34 CORRECT (the guessed owner does declare the method), 15 WRONG (it does not; typically an external interface declares it instead, e.g. `JdkVersionDTO extends Linkable implements Named, Described, Selectable<T>` guessing `Linkable.getLabel` where Linkable declares only getLinks/addLink and Selectable declares getLabel), and 33 unverifiable because the owner is itself outside the repo. That is 30.6% of the VERIFIABLE guesses. Suppressing the tier was considered and rejected on the evidence: it would remove the 15 wrong edges AND the 34 right ones, because the two are indistinguishable at analysis time — passes 1 and 2 have already walked the whole hierarchy and found no declarer, so every remaining candidate is equally unproven, and no ordering of them can be justified from one file. The tier is already below the 0.7 fabrication threshold, so these are declared suspicion rather than counted relationships. What was missing is that nothing EXERCISED it: the tier is reachable from a single-file fixture (the ancestor only has to be absent from that file), so the absence was a gap in the fixture lane rather than a property of the tier. Pinned now by `java/override-guess-tier`, which asserts the guess edge together with its `reasonCode` and forbids the documented NEGATIVE — an un-annotated method must produce no guess, since guessing there would fabricate an override that is really an overload. Proven load-bearing: disabling the tier fails the fixture (java 46/47), restored 47/47. A consumer that wants only resolved overrides should filter on `reasonCode`, not on a magic 0.5.

decisions.question: The F8 census injects ERROR and MISSING into every language's node-type set by hand (completeness-inventory.ts:609 — they are not in the wasm symbol table), yet no java spec row claimed them, so section-a failed for java on the same pair that fails 10+ other lanes. Gap, silent omission, or handled?
decisions.decision: RULED — HANDLED, following the precedent the gate itself names. completeness-inventory.ts:601-608 cites bash BD5: 'a spec that classifies ERROR — correctly, since the analyzer consults it — was being told its own row was grammar drift ... the fix is never to delete the correct row.' java holds the same EXPLICIT guard the JVM family uses, at real-java-analyzer.ts:221 — `if (node.type === "ERROR" || node.type === "MISSING")` — which records a diagnostic on result.errors and skips the damaged subtree. So ERROR is handled_verified and MISSING is internal_silent, the same split bash and javascript use. Measured on the pinned grammar: a wholly damaged file yields symbols=[] with one diagnostic per ERROR; a clean file yields none. And the guard is SCOPED, never a blanket file refusal — the property BD5 insists on, because a blanket refusal swallows valid declarations in a partially broken file. Verified: `class Good { void ok(){} } class Bad { void m( { int x = ; }` still yields Good, ok, Bad and m, with exactly one diagnostic. No fabrication is possible here: an unresolved name stays unresolved.

label_coverage._description: Which relationship labels this lane actually COMPARES, and which admitted labels have no oracle behind them. Measured by script/m14/verify-label-coverage.ts and script/m14/verify-truth-existence.ts.

declared_no_truth.label: overrides
declared_no_truth.reason: `overrides` sits in the differential allowlist DEFAULT admitted prefix for every language except csharp/dart/swift/cpp, so it is compared for this lane — but this lane has no overrides oracle, so every analyzer overrides row enters the comparison with no truth to meet and is counted as an unexplained FABRICATION. That number accuses the analyzer of inventing edges when the real gap is that nobody wrote down what it should have produced. Dropping the label instead would hide the analyzer's output, which is the other half of the same silence. Closes when an overrides oracle exists for this language (scala's own cross-file work is recorded as SDJ-8); until then the state is DECLARED rather than counted as a verdict.
declared_no_truth.closes_when: an overrides oracle exists for this language; then admit it and reconcile
